channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Adopting a New Criminal Code After 105 Amendments
item.description: Kazakhstan is evaluating the necessity of a new Criminal Code, considering the 105 amendments made to the existing one over the past decade. The discussion centers on whether the current legal framework adequately addresses contemporary challenges or if a comprehensive revision is required.

item.title: Tajikistan Police Search for Missing 17-Year-Old Girl
item.description: Police in Tajikistan's Jaloliddin Balkhi district are searching for Farishtamokh Muidinovna Zoirova, born in 2008, who went missing on September 13, 2026. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported she left her home in Ittifok village and has not been seen since. Authorities are appealing for public assistance.

item.title: Kazakhstan Declares National Day of Mourning After Naval Exercise Tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan declared September 25, 2026, a national day of mourning following the deaths of 14 servicemen during naval exercises in the Mangystau region. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev expressed condolences and ordered an investigation into the incident, which occurred due to severe weather conditions on the Caspian Sea coast.

item.title: Almaty Announces New Water Tariffs Effective October 1
item.description: Starting October 1, Almaty residents will pay 178.06 tenge per cubic meter for cold water and 119.46 tenge for wastewater. New tariffs for consumers without meters and for street hydrants are also detailed. Rates for legal entities and state institutions will also change.

item.title: Prosecutor's Assistant in Tashkent Region Suspected of Demanding $12,000 Bribe
item.description: A prosecutor's assistant in the Okkurgan district of Tashkent region has been detained on suspicion of demanding a $12,000 bribe. The official allegedly promised to help resolve a car sale issue and secure a preferential loan. He was apprehended while receiving $4,700, with prior receipt of $1,300 confirmed.

item.title: Li Auto to begin vehicle assembly in Kazakhstan this autumn
item.description: Li Auto will commence vehicle production in Kazakhstan this autumn, starting with large-node assembly and potentially moving to small-node assembly. Kazakhstan is the first country outside China to produce the brand's hybrid models L6, L7, and L9 at the SaryarkaAvtoProm plant in Kostanay. The plant aims to produce up to 10,000 vehicles annually.

item.title: Sole survivor of Caspian Sea naval exercise tragedy stable in hospital
item.description: The sole surviving serviceman from a naval exercise tragedy on the Caspian Sea is in stable condition and receiving treatment. Twelve servicemen died and three were rescued after being swept into open water during a storm on September 24. A government commission is investigating the incident, and a criminal case has been opened.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Fund to Support Families of Deceased Servicemen
item.description: The Mangystau regional administration has opened a special account to assist families of fallen soldiers. Citizens and organizations wishing to contribute can find official details online. The "Ulyttyq Rux" foundation will manage these funds to prevent fraud. Kazakhstan declared September 25 a national day of mourning following the incident.

item.title: KazMunayGas to Provide Assistance to Families of Servicemen Lost at Sea
item.description: KazMunayGas (KMG) has expressed condolences and pledged necessary support to the families of servicemen who died during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Among the deceased was the son of a "OzenMunaiService" employee. The company stated that all necessary assistance will be provided to the families.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reduces Coal Imports by Nearly 60 Percent
item.description: In the first seven months of 2026, Kyrgyzstan's coal trade generated $51.89 million in net profit. This was driven by a surge in lignite exports to Tajikistan and China, coupled with a significant reduction in imports from Kazakhstan. Stone coal imports decreased by 71.4% in value.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission approves media accreditation rules for elections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission (CEC) has approved regulations for accrediting media and online publications during elections and referendums. A specialized automated system will be implemented to digitalize accreditation procedures, streamlining application processing, verification, and information publication for increased transparency and efficiency.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission approves budget for presidential elections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission has approved a budget of 1.2 billion soms for the upcoming presidential elections, with funds allocated for 2026 and 2027. The budget includes provisions for potential repeat voting, overseas voting, and operational costs for polling stations, including those abroad and remote voting sites.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Approves FinTech Strategy Through 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has approved a national strategy for financial technology development until 2030. The plan aims to make Uzbekistan the most favorable jurisdiction for fintech companies in Central Asia by 2030, ensuring digital finance is safe and accessible. Key phases include infrastructure development, launching Open Banking, and integrating digital identification and payment systems.

item.title: Cold Water and Sewerage Tariffs to Increase in Almaty from October
item.description: Almaty will see increased tariffs for cold water supply and sewerage starting October 1. The new price for residents will be 297.52 tenge per cubic meter for both services combined. This represents a significant rise from last year's tariffs. New rates for legal entities and state institutions are also published.

item.title: Former Deputy Interior Minister Bekmurod Abdullayev Appointed Head of Chilonzor District Police
item.description: Former Deputy Interior Minister Bekmurod Abdullayev has been appointed head of the Chilonzor district police department. He previously served as deputy interior minister and head of public security services. Abdullayev was previously investigated for embezzlement of budget funds but was later released from custody.

item.title: Bodies of Two More Soldiers Drowned in Caspian Sea Found; Search Officially Concluded
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense confirmed the recovery of the bodies of two more servicemen, Sergeant Mansur Gumarov and sailor Miras Turdybekuly, bringing the total number of confirmed deaths to 14. Three soldiers were rescued. The search operations have officially concluded.

item.title: Two more servicemen found dead after Caspian Sea exercise incident
item.description: The bodies of two more servicemen, swept into the Caspian Sea during exercises in the Mangystau region, have been recovered. The Ministry of Defense reported that the death toll has now reached 14 people.

item.title: Father of survivor rescued from Caspian Sea details son's ordeal and recovery
item.description: The father of a serviceman rescued from the Caspian Sea shared details of his son's survival and recovery. The soldier, who swam ashore and searched for a comrade, is in stable condition and expected to remain hospitalized until October 3.

item.title: Soldier Surviving Caspian Sea Military Exercise Recovers in Hospital
item.description: A soldier who survived a military exercise in the Caspian Sea is recovering in the therapy department of a hospital in Mangystau region. Akzhol Temiraliev was transferred from intensive care after his condition improved. His parents visited him, and a blogger recorded a video. The soldier is currently unable to provide full details due to an ongoing investigation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Mandates Disclosure of Uranium Asset Control Changes Amid Rosatom Deals
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced a requirement for companies to disclose changes in control over uranium assets. This measure comes in the context of ongoing deals with Russia's Rosatom, highlighting increased scrutiny over strategic resource ownership and foreign investment in the sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan Declares National Day of Mourning for Military Personnel Lost in Mangystau
item.description: Kazakhstan has declared September 25, 2026, a national day of mourning for military personnel who died during exercises in the Mangystau region. The announcement recalls major tragic events in recent years, including mine collapses and fires, that resulted in significant loss of life.

item.title: Criminal Charges Filed in Kazakhstan Military Deaths in Mangystau Region
item.description: Criminal cases have been initiated in Kazakhstan under articles concerning negligence and violation of navigation rules following the deaths of military personnel near Aktau. A government commission is investigating the incident, and families of the deceased will receive state support.

item.title: Uzbekistan Power System Failure Causes Blackouts in Southern Kazakhstan
item.description: A power system failure in Uzbekistan on September 25 caused significant blackouts in southern Kazakhstan. A loss of 1,516 megawatts of generation in Uzbekistan led to an unexpected separation of the North-South transit in the Central Asian power grid. Power supply was restored within an hour.

item.title: SCAT Airlines to Launch Charter Flights from Bishkek to Sanya
item.description: SCAT Airlines will commence direct charter flights between Bishkek and Sanya starting in early December. This new route, scheduled for the 2026/2027 winter season, aims to facilitate travel for Kyrgyz passengers to the popular Chinese tourist destination without requiring transfers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Tariff Moratorium Allows Increases in Special Cases
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved a procedure for tariff increases during the existing moratorium. The Antimonopoly Service will review applications, assessing economic justification and compliance with presidential decree exceptions. Final decisions rest with tariff-setting bodies, considering the service's conclusion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan introduces special order for state bond-financed construction projects
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President has introduced a temporary special order for state treasury bonds used to finance construction, capital repair, and reconstruction. From February 1 to December 31, 2026, funds from bond placements will not be counted in the republican budget. Construction financing will occur outside the Unified Treasury Account and budget expenditures.

item.title: 80 UN member states condemn Iran, demand reopening of Hormuz Strait
item.description: Eighty UN member states have condemned Iran and demanded the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain's foreign minister stated that the actions of Tehran and its Houthi allies threaten global trade and energy security. The statement was made at the UN.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened After Military Personnel Deaths During Training Exercise
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Mangystau region following the deaths of military personnel during a training exercise. An interdepartmental investigative team is examining the incident, which involved 17 servicemen being swept into the sea due to severe weather. Twelve died, three were rescued, and two remain missing.

item.title: Details Emerge on Condition of Injured Serviceman in Mangystau
item.description: Information has become available regarding the condition of a military serviceman who was injured in Mangystau. Further details on the incident and the serviceman's health status are expected.

item.title: Nine Kazakhstan Servicemen Die During Caspian Sea Naval Exercises
item.description: Nine Kazakhstani servicemen died during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea off the coast of Mangystau region on September 24, 2026. The Ministry of Defense reported that 19 servicemen were swept into the sea due to adverse weather conditions. Three were rescued, one hospitalized, and searches for the others continue.

item.title: Kazakhstan to increase Russian gas imports amid potential US sanctions
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to boost natural gas imports from Russia under a new agreement with Gazprom. The deal involves purchasing approximately 11 billion cubic meters of gas this year, with further talks for 2027. This move comes as Kazakhstan faces surging domestic demand despite being a net exporter, and as Russia faces potential US sanctions on its energy sector.

item.title: Russia instigates trade disputes within Eurasian Economic Union
item.description: Russia is reportedly initiating trade conflicts with fellow Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) members, including Kazakhstan and Armenia, while engaged in military actions in Ukraine. These actions contradict the EAEU's aim of promoting free trade. Moscow has imposed trade bans on Armenian goods and cut off gas supplies, citing Armenia's closer ties with the European Union.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Orders Investigation into Soldier Deaths
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev chaired a commission meeting following the deaths of servicemen during military exercises in the Mangystau region. A criminal case has been initiated, and an interdepartmental investigative team is working to establish the circumstances and identify those responsible. Families of the deceased will receive state support.

item.title: US and Uzbekistan to cooperate on nuclear energy safety and operations
item.description: The United States and Uzbekistan signed a memorandum of understanding to cooperate on nuclear energy operations and safety issues. The agreement covers monitoring, safe operations, disaster response, and improving regulatory guidelines and training programs.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans Caspian and Black Sea logistics hubs for Middle Corridor trade
item.description: Uzbekistan intends to establish logistics facilities on the Caspian and Black Seas to support its Middle Corridor trade agenda. Agreements are in place for facilities in Georgia's Poti port, with plans to develop infrastructure in Aktau, Turkmenbashi, and Baku.

item.title: Kremlin sends congratulatory note to Armenia's Pashinyan on Independence Day
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin sent a congratulatory note to Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Armenia's 35th anniversary of re-independence. The message, also echoed by other Russian officials, emphasized maintaining comprehensive Russian-Armenian cooperation.

item.title: Uzbek Company Mega Plast Group Focuses on High-Quality Polyethylene Pipes for Infrastructure
item.description: Uzbekistan's Mega Plast Group produces high-pressure polyethylene pipes and drip irrigation systems for water supply, energy, and agriculture. The company, operating since 2016, emphasizes product quality and increased production volume. They have secured credit funds and purchased new equipment to meet growing demand.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets BlackRock Leadership in New York to Discuss Tashkent Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration, met with BlackRock executives in New York to discuss establishing the Tashkent International Financial Center by 2027. Discussions also covered Uzbekistan's development prospects, with Mirziyoyeva noting the country is becoming a hub for significant investments.

item.title: Russian President Putin Expresses Condolences to Kazakhstan Over Sailor Deaths in Caspian Sea
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin sent condolences to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev following a tragic incident during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Seventeen Kazakh sailors were swept out to sea in bad weather; twelve died, three were rescued, and two remain missing. Criminal cases have been opened.

item.title: Uzbekistan prioritizes education as key to national development and human capital
item.description: Uzbekistan's government views education and youth intellectual development as a crucial long-term investment. President outlined seven national programs to boost the country's development, focusing on strengthening economic and social potential. Knowledge and skills are identified as the primary capital for future growth, with a focus on quality education and teacher development.
